title: Oura to acquire AI-native primary care startup Counsel Health for $625M
content:
Oura announced on Tuesday that it’s acquiring AI-native primary care company Counsel Health for $625 million. The deal comes a few weeks after Oura postponed its up to $2.2 billion IPO indefinitely, citing “uncertainty in the IPO market.”
Counsel Health is an AI-powered healthcare platform that combines a chat-based medical experience with access to licensed physicians. Its service was integrated into the Oura app in June.
Users can connect with Counsel’s medical AI to get personalized medical advice, and chat with a physician when needed, all within the Oura app. Now, the companies plan to expand on their existing partnership to build across preventative care, acute care, and specialty and chronic care.
While Oura has largely dominated the smart ring market for years, rivals like RingConn and Ultrahuman are emerging to dethrone it, putting pressure on the company to keep innovating. By acquiring Counsel Health, Oura is looking to expand its business and help users access medical care.
“Oura helps members understand their physiology and, with Counsel, they can take action on their health across a range of needs, from quick questions and prescriptions to lab results, chronic care, and referrals,” said Oura CEO Tom Hale in a press release.
Counsel Health raised a $25 million Series A a year ago, led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and GV. PitchBook estimates it had raised a total of $36 million.
Following the acquisition, Oura says Counsel will continue serving existing and new enterprise partners, with the goal of expanding its AI-native care model to more people beyond Oura’s membership.
Counsel CEO Muthu Alagappan will join Oura as chief clinical AI officer, alongside the company’s 70 employees, Bloomberg reports.
“At Counsel, we’ve built medical AI around trust, safety and responsibility, keeping physicians in the loop for clinical decisions,” Alagappan said in the press release. “Oura’s data gives clinicians objective context, trended biometrics, and member engagement to deliver more informed care. From the start, our teams bonded over a joint vision, shared culture, and mission, further solidifying as we negotiated our deal over the past few months.”
The deal is expected to close before the end of 2027.
Oura also announced that its revenue grew 153% year-over-year to $533 million for the quarter ended on September 30. For its fiscal year 2026, Oura generated revenue of approximately $1.75 billion, marking 92% year-over-year growth.
The company reached an $11 billion valuation following a $900 million late-stage funding round in October 2025.

report.summary: Oura will acquire AI-native primary care startup Counsel Health for $625M to turn smart-ring health data into accessible medical care.
report.background: Oura has long led the smart-ring market, but rivals such as RingConn and Ultrahuman are gaining ground, pressuring it to move beyond tracking into healthcare services. The acquisition follows Oura's indefinite postponement of an IPO of up to $2.2 billion, citing uncertain markets, and comes as wearables shift from fitness metrics toward clinical-grade insights and remote care. Counsel Health combines a chat-based medical AI with access to licensed physicians; its service was integrated into the Oura app in June. Counsel had raised a $25 million Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz and GV, and about $36 million total. The deal signals Oura's push to build a preventive and chronic-care business around its biometric data.
key_points: Oura is paying $625 million for Counsel Health, an AI-primary-care platform that pairs medical AI chat with licensed physicians. Counsel will keep serving enterprise partners after the deal, which is expected to close before the end of 2027. Counsel CEO Muthu Alagappan will join Oura as chief clinical AI officer, along with its 70 employees.

The companies plan to expand their existing June integration beyond quick questions and prescriptions into preventative care, acute care, specialty care, and chronic care. Oura users will be able to get personalized medical advice and chat with a physician inside the Oura app, using ring data as clinical context for more informed decisions.

The deal comes after Oura postponed its IPO and faces rising smart-ring competition. Oura reported 153% year-over-year revenue growth to $533 million for the quarter ended September 30 and about $1.75 billion for fiscal 2026. It reached an $11 billion valuation after a $900 million late-stage round in October 2025.

Counsel emphasizes trust, safety, and physician oversight, keeping clinicians in the loop for clinical decisions. Oura frames its biometric data as objective context and trended signals that can help clinicians deliver more informed care. The acquisition aims to extend Counsel's AI-native care model beyond Oura members to more people and enterprise partners.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the deal validates vertical AI acquisitions that combine consumer hardware data with clinical services and human oversight, rather than standalone chatbots. It pushes wearables from monitoring into care delivery, raising the bar for evidence, safety, and regulatory compliance. Developers will see opportunities in wearable-data APIs, FHIR-based records, clinical workflow integration, and human-in-the-loop AI agents, but must handle privacy and liability carefully. Regular users may gain convenient triage, prescriptions, lab reviews, and referrals through a familiar app, plus more personalized advice from continuous biometrics. The risks include data privacy, potential overdiagnosis, cost transparency, and overreliance on AI, so physician oversight and clear boundaries will remain essential.
report.tools: Watch Oura's app integration and developer API, Counsel Health's clinical AI model, and enterprise care partnerships. For follow-up, open-source options include Medplum for FHIR-based healthcare backends, Fasten Health for patient-record aggregation, Open Health Stack for mobile clinical tools, and Apple HealthKit or Google Health Connect for wearable data. To prototype physician-in-the-loop chat workflows, developers can use LangGraph or CrewAI alongside FHIR terminology servers and clinical safety evaluation frameworks.
